docz-api webhook deliveries fail

GitHub delivers installation, installation_repositories, and push events to docz-api's POST /webhooks/github. Each accepted delivery enqueues an ingest, and the worker then refetches the repository. This runbook finds where a delivery stopped: at the edge before it reached docz-api, at docz-api's signature check, or in the ingest the delivery queued.

RUNBOOK-0002 Draft Donald Gifford 2026-10-01

Overview

Last Verified

Date PR Commit Verified by

Notes: Not yet run end to end. Written from deploy/tailscale-operator.md and INV-0007's failure drill.

Overview

Service: docz-api (charts/docz, the api workload)

Owner: @donaldgifford

When to Use

  • The GitHub App's Recent Deliveries page shows failed deliveries
  • A push to a repository's docs/ did not appear in docz-site
  • DoczAPIIngestFailures fires

Prerequisites

  • Admin on the GitHub App, for its settings page, Recent Deliveries, and the webhook secret
  • kubectl access to the namespace docz is installed in
  • For the Tailscale edge: admin on the tailnet, for its policy file and DNS settings
  • docz-api running with LOG_FORMAT=json, so its logs can be filtered with jq

Procedures

Procedures

Procedure 1: Redeliver and confirm

After a fix, replay the failed delivery and follow it through docz-api.

Steps
  1. 1.1 In the GitHub App's settings, open Advanced, then Recent Deliveries. Pick the failed delivery and choose Redeliver. Note its delivery ID (the X-GitHub-Delivery header).
  2. 1.2 Find the delivery in docz-api's logs. 
    kubectl -n docz logs deploy/docz-api --since 10m \
  | jq -c 'select(.delivery == "<delivery-id>" or (.msg | test("webhook|ingest job")))'

    Expected: no webhook signature verification failed line, and an ingest job enqueued line for the repository

  3. 1.3 Follow the ingest the delivery queued to the end. 
    kubectl -n docz logs deploy/docz-api --since 10m \
  | jq -c 'select(.repo == "<owner>/<name>")'

    Expected: processing ingest job, then ingest job complete

Verification
  • GitHub shows the redelivery with a 202
  • docz-site shows the change the delivery was for
Rollback

Rollback

  1. 1.R1 Not applicable: redelivery is idempotent. A replayed delivery ID is answered 200 and does no work.

Scenarios

Troubleshooting

GitHub reports a TLS EOF on every delivery
Symptom
GitHub reports a TLS EOF on every delivery
Alert
none; GitHub's Recent Deliveries shows the failure
Likely cause
the Tailscale Funnel cannot serve TLS. Either the proxy's tag lacks the funnel node attribute, or the tailnet has HTTPS certificates turned off
Steps
  1. S1.1 Diagnose: confirm nothing reached docz-api. A TLS EOF fails before HTTP, so there is no webhook log line for the delivery's time. 
    kubectl -n docz logs deploy/docz-api --since 30m | jq -c 'select(.msg | test("webhook"))'

    Expected: nothing near the failed delivery's timestamp

  2. S1.2 Diagnose: check Funnel on the operator's proxy pod. 
    kubectl -n tailscale exec <proxy-pod> -- tailscale funnel status

    Expected: a Funnel entry for the docz-api host. An empty result means the grant is missing

  3. S1.3 Resolve: add the funnel attribute for the proxy's tag in the tailnet policy file. 
    "nodeAttrs": [
  { "target": ["tag:k8s"], "attr": ["funnel"] }
]
  4. S1.4 Resolve: in the admin console, open DNS, then HTTPS Certificates, and turn them on.
  5. S1.5 Run Procedure 1.
The Ingress has no hostname
Symptom
The Ingress has no hostname
Alert
none; the GitHub App's webhook URL does not resolve
Likely cause
the Tailscale operator could not create the proxy for api.ingress
Steps
  1. S2.1 Diagnose: read the Ingress status. 
    kubectl -n docz get ingress docz-api -o jsonpath='{.status.loadBalancer.ingress}'

    Expected: a *.ts.net hostname. Empty means no proxy

  2. S2.2 Diagnose: read the operator's logs for the Ingress. 
    kubectl -n tailscale logs deploy/operator --since 1h | grep -i docz-api
  3. S2.3 Resolve: fix what the operator reports. It is usually its OAuth client or the tags it may assign. Then check that the hostname appears.
  4. S2.4 Resolve: set the GitHub App's webhook URL to https://<tls-host>.<tailnet>.ts.net/webhooks/github, then run Procedure 1.
Deliveries are answered 401
Symptom
Deliveries are answered 401
Alert
none; GitHub shows 401 responses
Likely cause
the GitHub App's webhook secret differs from the one docz-api holds, so the HMAC check fails before any work is done
Steps
  1. S3.1 Diagnose: find the verification failures. 
    kubectl -n docz logs deploy/docz-api --since 1h \
  | jq -c 'select(.msg == "webhook signature verification failed")'

    Expected: one line per failed delivery

  2. S3.2 Resolve: set one new secret in both places. Put it in the GitHub App's settings, then in the chart's api.secrets.webhookSecret, or in the existingSecret the release uses.
  3. S3.3 Resolve: roll the API so it reads the new secret, then run Procedure 1. 
    kubectl -n docz rollout restart deploy/docz-api
kubectl -n docz rollout status deploy/docz-api
Deliveries succeed but the change never appears
Symptom
Deliveries succeed but the change never appears
Alert
DoczAPIIngestFailures
Likely cause
the ingest the delivery queued is failing. Usually the cause is a malformed .docz.yaml at HEAD, or the GitHub App lacking access to the repository
Steps
  1. S4.1 Diagnose: confirm the push was one docz-api acts on. Only a push to the default branch that touches .docz.yaml, docs/, or a watched file enqueues an ingest. A push for a repository that was never onboarded logs push for unknown repo; skipping until onboarded.
  2. S4.2 Diagnose: read the failed attempts. Each one logs its cause. 
    kubectl -n docz logs deploy/docz-api --since 1h \
  | jq -c 'select(.msg == "ingest job attempt failed") | {repo, reason, retried, max_retry, err}'

    Expected: the err field names the cause

  3. S4.3 Resolve: fix the cause at its source. Fix the .docz.yaml and push, or grant the App access to the repository. A new push re-enqueues the ingest.
A repository stopped re-ingesting after repeated failures
Symptom
A repository stopped re-ingesting after repeated failures
Alert
DoczAPIIngestFailures, then silence
Likely cause
the ingest exhausted its retries. Since INV-0007 the next trigger clears the finished task and re-enqueues, so a new push or delivery is all it takes
Steps
  1. S5.1 Diagnose: confirm the task was exhausted rather than still retrying. 
    kubectl -n docz logs deploy/docz-api --since 24h \
  | jq -c 'select(.component == "asynq" and (.msg | test("Retry exhausted")))'
  2. S5.2 Resolve: fix the cause, as in the previous scenario.
  3. S5.3 Resolve: run Procedure 1. The re-enqueue logs cleared a finished ingest task and re-enqueued with the cleared_state it removed.

Escalation

Who When How
@donaldgifford A cause not listed here, or a fix that does not hold GitHub issue on donaldgifford/docz
